text:
**For most UK sole traders and very small businesses, I’d start by comparing Starling, Mettle and Monzo Business Lite.** They all have no monthly fee on their free plans; the best fit depends mainly on cash deposits, accounting tools and how you like to bank.

| Account | Could suit you if… | Points to check |
|---|---|---|
| **Starling Business** | You want a free digital account, unlimited UK transfers and links to accounting software such as Xero, QuickBooks or FreeAgent. | Cash deposits at the Post Office cost 0.7% (minimum £3); no branch counter service. |
| **Mettle by NatWest** | You want a free account with bookkeeping features and FreeAgent included. | Check eligibility and whether its features suit your business; it’s app-based. |
| **Monzo Business Lite** | You want a straightforward app-based account and don’t need accounting-software integrations on the free plan. | Cash deposits cost £1; the paid plan adds features. |
| **Tide** | You value invoicing and business admin tools. | Its free plan has transaction charges: the comparison found five free UK transfers a month, then 20p each; cash deposits also cost extra. |
| **A high-street bank, such as Lloyds** | You regularly deposit cash or cheques, or want branch access. | Lloyds advertises 12 months free, then £10/month; cash and cheque transactions can cost extra. |

**My quick pick:** Starling for a simple, free everyday business account; Mettle if FreeAgent is useful; and a high-street bank if you rely on cash or in-person service. Compare the *ongoing* costs, not just introductory offers—especially cash deposits, payment volumes, international transactions and any paid bookkeeping plan.

One caveat: a sole trader isn’t always required to have a separate business account, but keeping business and personal transactions separate can make bookkeeping and tax records much easier. If you’re a **limited company**, use an account intended for business rather than a personal current account.

Fees and features can change, so check the provider’s current tariff and eligibility before applying.
